Aims and Ethos
Statement of Ethos and Values
Links Primary School offers all children a high standard of academic and social education, enabling and challenging all pupils to reach their full potential. We provide a safe, secure and stimulating environment in which we encourage all children to value themselves and others. We help them to make the right choices and develop into responsible and caring members of society.

Welcome
For over 113 years, Links Primary School has been a cornerstone of education for children in Tooting and the surrounding areas.
At Links, our children are at the heart of everything we do. We are dedicated to providing an outstanding education in a nurturing community that values and respects each child’s unique qualities. Our passionate and dedicated staff ensure that every child thrives academically while also developing their individual talents and strengths. We take great pride in our students and the inclusive, supportive environment we foster alongside their families.
While our website offers a glimpse into life at Links, the best way to experience our school is to visit in person. We warmly invite you to arrange a visit through the school office.
We look forward to welcoming you to the Links community.
Natalie Anderson and Vicki Murray (Heads of School )

pageCache.text:
Welcome to Links
By our school council
Hello! Welcome to Links Primary School! We are so happy you’re here.
Our school is a place where everyone can learn, play, and be themselves. There are so many fun things to do, from creative art and exciting science experiments to sports and music.
The teachers and staff are really kind and helpful, and they make sure we all feel safe and happy at school. If you ever need help, there’s always someone to talk to.
We have lots of friends here, and we love making new ones! There are big playgrounds to run on, quiet corners to read in, and clubs after school where you can try something new.
At Links, we look after each other. We follow our rules so everyone can feel safe and respected. We celebrate each other’s achievements, help each other when we are stuck, and have fun together every day.
We can’t wait for you to join our school family, make new friends, and discover all the amazing things you can do at Links Primary!
From all of us at Links Primary School – welcome!

pageCache.text:
EXTENDED SERVICES HOME
Breakfast & After School Club
Our breakfast club and after school club are run by Raphel and his capable team. Raphel is committed to providing children with a safe, fun, and supportive environment where they can learn and grow. He has a team of experienced and caring staff who are committed to providing children with the best possible care.
Breakfast Club
Our breakfast club is a great way to start your day! We offer a variety of healthy and delicious breakfast options, including cereal, toast, fruit, and juice. The breakfast club is open from 7:30am. Breakfast is served between 7:55am and 8:25am.
We believe that starting your day with a healthy breakfast is essential for a productive day at school. Our breakfast club provides a safe and welcoming environment where children can enjoy a nutritious meal before the start of the school day.
We also offer a variety of activities for children to enjoy during breakfast club, such as reading, playing games, Colouring and some dancing. This helps to create a positive and fun atmosphere where children can socialize and make new friends.
If you are interested in enrolling your child in the breakfast club. Please fill out a booking form.
After School Club
Our after school club is a great way to keep your children safe and entertained after school. We provide a safe and welcoming environment where children can relax, play, and do their homework. We also offer a variety of activities, such as arts and crafts, sports, and games.
We collect children from class and take them to our after school club. The club is open from 3:15pm to 6:00pm. We serve tea between 4:45pm and 5:30pm, followed by a dessert. We cater to all dietary requirements.
We also have an outdoor play area where children can run around and burn off some energy. We believe that it is important for children to have time to play and be active, and our outdoor play area provides the perfect opportunity for them to do just that.
If you are looking for a safe and fun after school club for your children, then we would be happy to welcome you to ours. Please fill out a booking form.
Pricing and Times
To make things simple, you can pre book sessions up to 24 hours before they begin. If you need to make a last-minute booking, please note there may be a late fee depending on the circumstances.
Breakfast Club: Booking closes 24 hours before the session starts, at 7:30 am the day before.
Breakfast Club (7:30 am - 8:40 am)
After School Club: Booking closes 24 hours before the session starts, at 3:15 pm the day before.
After School Club (3:15 pm - 6:00 pm)
Bookings made after the deadlines won't be possible via the app. To make a late booking, you must email or call us (we do not accept bookings via text or WhatsApp). You will be charged the After Booking Closes Price. Please ensure any outstanding balances are cleared before booking additional sessions.

Sport
Physical Education and Sport
At Links, Physical Education (PE) and Sport have always been highly valued elements of the curriculum. Mr Roughley and all of the staff believe that through participation in competitive sport and taking part in regular PE lessons, young people learn about and begin to recognise the value of core life skills such as teamwork, fair play and respect for themselves and others.
Sport has been shown to have a positive effect on children's physical and mental health as well as on their growth and development while also providing a controlled, healthy environment for young people to learn about winning and losing.
With rising obesity rates evident in the borough of Merton and with the limited space in which children can undertake exercise, our duty as a school is to ensure that your children are given opportunities to take part in sports and games that they would otherwise not have access to.
The Merton School Sport Partnership
Links is a proud supporter of the Merton School Sport Partnership who coordinate both cluster and borough-wide competitions for children of all ages throughout the year. The MSSP also provide Preparation, Planning and Assessment (PPA) cover for teachers (Tuesday- Thursday) and support teachers in their continuing professional development.
In 2015/2016, Links received a certificate from the MSSP in recognition of the fact that they were the only school out of 43 in the borough that had entered every event. This commitment to sport and PE is something of which the school is very proud and we will continue to give children as many opportunities as we are able.
In addition to the above services, the MSSP offer a wide range of CPD programmes, support schools in achieving the targets set in their action plans and oversee and award the MSSP Sports Mark. They provide links between schools and local clubs offering children who show outstanding promise, opportunities to take their promise further.

pageCache.text:
Sport at Links
At Links we are passionate about the role sport plays in child development. We are a member of Merton School Sports Partnership (MSSP), with whom we work closely in developing and providing a wide range of high quality sporting experiences for all our children. All year groups have access to 2 hours of high quality PE lessons per week, one lesson of which is led by the class teacher and the other of which is led by a sports specialist from the partnership. Children also have access to a wide range of extra-curricular sporting experiences.
This year we are proud to say that we were awarded the MSSP Platinum Award, recognising our consistent Gold Awards over recent years. This reflects our commitment to PE and Sport at Links, and the hard work put in by all children and staff to ensure this remains a key focus of the school.
We follow MSSP’s PE scheme of work, which has been developed and refined by a range of experienced professionals and offers a development of skills both within and across year groups. Lessons cover a wide range of sports and physical activities, and are designed to cater for and develop a variety of skills, abilities and interests.
Children in Year 4 attend a 2 week, intensive, daily lesson, taught by professionals at Canons Leisure Centre. Children who are still unable to swim the 25 metres required by the end of Key Stage 2 are then offered top up lessons in Year 5 (in the form of a 1 week, intensive, daily lesson) to give them the best opportunity to learn this valuable skill.
Click here to read more information on swimming.
Here at Links we are keen to enter teams into a wide range of sporting competitions, giving opportunities to children throughout the school. This ranges from ‘best team’ events, designed for children who are keen to compete at a challenging level against their peers from other schools in the borough, to ‘participation’ events which give children an opportunity to discover and enjoy new sports. Our aim is that by the end of Year 6, all children have been given the opportunity to represent the school on at least one occasion. In addition to this, we have introduced a house system at Links which we are beginning to use to develop our provision for competitive intra-school sport.
As part of our commitment to competitive sport, we place a strong emphasis on ‘Refspect’, ensuring all children understand that sport is about more than our ability to compete, but rather our ability to encourage, support and work as a team, including how to be both good winners and good losers. We are immensely proud to say that in 2017/18 we were awarded the overall RefSpect Award from MSSP, as we received the most nominations of any school in the borough.
At Links we offer a range of sporting clubs and opportunities, supported by a number of high-quality outside providers. These include:

Governors
Message from our Governors
On behalf of Links Primary School, welcome to our website.
At Links Primary School our children are happy, enthusiastic, unique individuals eager to learn and taking pride in achieving high standards in their accomplishments. They are fully supported and encouraged to flourish by our incredible staff who are both dedicated to educational excellence whilst creating a safe and nurturing environment for all. Links is a fantastic community school which feels like a family.
Our parents are also hugely supportive of the school and their children's education, both at home and through volunteering at the school. We are also extremely thankful to have a highly motivated PTA, organising popular, fun and well attended events raising a considerable amount of money, benefitting the school and its pupils.
At Links Primary School, our experienced and tenacious Governing Board works in collaboration with the school focussing on improving standards and striving for best practice both in and outside of the classroom. We ensure we stay updated on and apply new legislation through regular training programmes both in person and online. Effective governance is beyond simply attending meetings. You'll find our governors are visible, assisting with many school events taking place throughout the year.
Governors are present for classes monitoring the impact of the teaching on our pupils, special assemblies, inset and training days, inspections, and LEA reviews - to name but a few areas of our involvement. Governors are also involved strategically in all other aspects of the school from school meals to the general property management.
If you have a specific concern or complaint, in the first instance, we encourage you to speak to a teacher or head teacher. If any reason this is not possible, please speak to a governor. All governors can be contacted via the school office.
Current parents are welcome to contact governors with questions or feedback. We encourage any prospective parents who are thinking of sending their children to Links to browse through our comprehensive website and, more importantly, take time to visit our school to see firsthand what Links really has to offer.
We are very pleased to welcome you to Links Primary School.

Attendance & Punctuality
Attendance & Punctuality: A Parents and Carers Guide
Helping your child attend school regularly and arrive on time is one of the most important ways you can support their learning, happiness, wellbeing and development.
Every school day matters. Being in school regularly helps children build strong relationships, develop confidence and make steady progress with their learning. We understand that sometimes children and families may face challenges that can make attending school difficult. If you have concerns about your child's attendance, please talk to us — we are here to help and support you.
Why Attendance Matters
As a parent or carer, helping your child attend school every day, wherever possible, gives them the best opportunity to learn, grow and enjoy their time at school.
Why Punctuality Matters
Arriving at school on time helps your child start the day positively. It means they can settle into their classroom, see their friends, listen to important morning information and begin their learning with everyone else.
Even being a few minutes late regularly can mean missing important parts of the school day.
Good attendance and punctuality help your child make the most of every school day. By working together, we can help every child feel happy, safe, included and ready to learn.
If you have any concerns about your child's attendance or punctuality, please speak to a member of the school team. We are always happy to listen and offer support.
These are important life skills that will help children grow and succeed. It’s important for parents to support their child by making sure they are at school and trying their best each day.
How Missed Days Can Affect Learning
It can be surprising to see how quickly missed school days can add up and how much learning a child can miss when their attendance falls.
95% Attendance - An attendance figure of 95% may sound very good, but over a school year it means a child has missed approximately 10 school days.
That is around two full weeks of learning.
During this time, your child could miss important teaching, new skills, classroom discussions, stories, practical activities and opportunities to learn and play with their friends.
90% Attendance - At 90% attendance, a child has missed approximately 20 school days over the course of a school year.
That is around four full weeks of learning.
This can make it more difficult for children to keep up with their class, particularly when learning builds on what has been taught previously.
85% Attendance - At 85% attendance, a child could miss approximately 30 school days over a school year.
That is around six full weeks of learning — more than a whole half-term.
When children miss this much school, they can miss a significant amount of learning and may need additional support to catch up.
Every School Day Counts
Every day in school provides children with opportunities to learn, practise new skills, develop friendships, build confidence and take part in the wider life of our school.
We understand that children will sometimes be unwell or have circumstances that prevent them from attending. However, where children are well enough to be in school, regular attendance and good punctuality help them make the most of every learning opportunity.
Every day matters. Every lesson counts. Every child deserves the opportunity to make the most of their time at school.
Celebrating Good Attendance and Punctuality.
At Links Primary, we celebrate good attendance and punctuality.
We also recognise the need to tackle any issues surrounding attendance and punctuality and for the last few years, we have been very successful. We have regular attendance panels and a proactive Education Welfare Officer. Research shows that when children miss a lot of school, it can affect how they feel about school and how much they learn and grow.
We are committed to meeting our obligation with regard to school attendance through our whole-school culture and ethos that values good attendance, including:
We will also promote and support punctuality in attending lessons.
Promoting good attendance
Reducing absence, including persistent and severe absence
Acting early to address patterns of absence
The School day:
Children should arrive at school by 8:45am. The school gates open at 8:35am, and children in Reception to Year 6 can go straight into class from then. If a child arrives after 8:45am, they will be marked as late. If a child has not arrived and been marked in the register by 9:30am, families will receive an email to check the reason for the absence.
Nursery children should arrive at nursery by 8:30am. Any nursery child who arrives after 8:40am, will need to go to the main school office on Frinton Road.
Illness:
NHS guidance on school absence can be found here.
Medical Absence:
Attending a medical or dental appointment will be counted as authorised as long as the pupil’s parent/carer notifies the school in advance of the appointment. However, we encourage parents/carers to make medical and dental appointments out of school hours where possible. Where this is not possible, the pupil should be out of school for the minimum amount of time necessary.
Special Leave Requests:
Children of school age who are registered at school must, by law, attend that school regularly. Regular attendance is important, not just because the law requires it but because it is the best way of ensuring that a child makes the most of the educational opportunities which are available to him/her. There may be occasions when a child has to miss school – for example, if he or she is unwell. Any other absence should be kept to an absolute minimum. In particular, parents must avoid taking their children out of school during term time to go on holiday. Satisfactory attendance is counted as attendance at or above 96%.
What the law says
The law makes it clear that parents do not have any right to take a child out of school for a term-time holiday except in exceptional circumstances. Headteachers can no longer authorise holiday leave during term time. At Links, governors have decided that these exceptional circumstances will only be considered if a child’s attendance is already at or above satisfactory attendance levels of 96% for the ‘rolling’ year prior to a special leave application being made.
The following reasons do not constitute an acceptable reason for leave to be granted during term time:~
Availability of cheap holidays
Availability of desired accommodation
Poor weather experienced during school holiday periods
How to apply for special leave during term time
Special Leave Request forms can be completed online via Leave of Absence Request Form.
This must be done at least 2 weeks in advance of your proposed leave dates. Fill in the form for the attention of the Headteacher. You should expect to hear from us within 7 working days. Term-time holidays cannot be granted unless there are exceptional circumstances that might justify it and evidence is provided accordingly.
What if I decide to go away anyway? - What will happen?
If you take your child out of school regardless, then this will be counted as unauthorised absence – this is the same as truancy and is treated in the same way – a referral to Education Welfare. Truancy is dealt with severely by the law and you risk a fine and prosecution.
For more information, please see our Attendance & Punctuality policy.

My Child At School
Welcome to our MCAS help page!
We’re excited to announce that we’re now using a new messaging system to streamline communication. We encourage all parents/carers to download the app to stay updated and receive important notifications in real-time. This will help ensure you don’t miss any critical information, trips, clubs and reminders.
Click the Logo below to login to MCAS (My Child At School)
MCAS is our school management information system. Through the parent account, parents can report an absence, view/amend contact details, book and pay for Breakfast Club, Afterschool Club and Playscheme sessions, Trips and Clubs. As well as contact and receive emails from the school (replacing ParentPay and Parentmail).
To register click on ReSet Password and enter the email address we have at school for you. The parent and/or carer with an account is responsible for managing their account for booking, amending, cancelling and ensuring adequate bookings are made in good time for wraparound care and lunch provision.
The My Child At School App, can be downloaded from the app/play store. Just use the email address that we have at school for you to register. The app is available in in lots of different languages, making it easier to communicate with our families whose first language isn’t English.
Receiving messages from school
These will appear in your Messages (envelope icon at top of the page to left of your Profile and name) and in Announcements.
Please ensure you have switched on notifications to alert you to these. If not, you will need to regularly check here for any new messages.
To Report an Absence
To report an absence on the MCAS (MyChildAtSchool) app, select Attendance from the dashboard, tap Report an Absence, and fill in the required dates and reason. Ensure you select the correct child, input the dates, and click "Send" to notify the school by 9 am.
To book School Dinners
Go to the Dinner Detail widget and click 'More' (this will open up the menu where you can make your selection) How to Book a School Meal on MCAS
To pay for School Dinners (Nursery Only)
On the Dinner Money widget, enter the amount you wish to pay in the Deposit Amount box
Click 'add to basket' and check out in the usual way. Please note, dinner money becomes due on the day lunch is taken so, you may wish to pay weekly or termly in advance if you do not pay in full at the time of booking.
To cancel a dinner booking (up to 1 day before)
Go to 'Dinner Detail' and click 'More'(as if you were booking a lunch).
Find the date you wish to cancel and use the clear button to unselect your choice.
To book Afterschool or Breakfast club
Select Breakfast & Afterschool Club from the left hand menu.
Select a club from the Available Wraparound Care Clubs by clicking on the magnifying glass.
Click on the session you wish to book. A pop up box will appear showing a summary of what you are about to book. If correct, proceed and enroll. (The wraparound care clubs screen now shows the sessions booked and costs with the option to Add to Basket. If paying with childcare vouchers you do not need to add to basket as your balance will be credited once we have received the voucher. If you are paying using a card, click add to basket and enter the amount you wish to pay off the balance. This can be full or part payment in line with our Terms & Conditions. Once you have made a booking, the club will move to the section above but you will follow the same process to make future bookings).
To cancel an Afterschool or Breakfast Club booking
From the Clubs & Trips widget click on black arrow next to the club.
Click on the magnifying glass next to the club.
Click on the session you wish to cancel – an X will now show.
Click Proceed to cancel the session.
(Refunds for cancelled sessions will automatically be refunded to the card used to make payment. If you have paid using childcare vouchers, your voucher balance will receive the credit. Please see our Terms and Conditions for more information).
To update your contact details
Select Data Collection Form from the right-hand menu. This will show the details we hold for your child
Click on the blue View your personal details button (top right) to switch to your information. This is where you can make amendments to your telephone number and email address. Any changes will then be approved by the school before your child’s record is updated.
To view your Payment history
Click on the drop down next to your name (top left).

Online Safety
Links Primary School believes strongly in the importance of computing and digital skills for your children and we are also dedicated to ensuring that they remain safe and responsible in an ever-changing online world. That's why we are a Digital Schools member of Parent Zone, an organisation dedicated to making the internet work for families. As a parent of a Digital School you are able to get access to a regular online safety magazine - Digital Parenting - which will be sent home with your child.
Parent Zone also run ParentInfo a website full of advice on parenting issues both online and offline. See below for a feed of the latest advice from ParentInfo.
We ask all children, young people and adults involved in the life of Links Primary School to sign an Acceptable Use Policy (AUP), which is a document that outlines how we expect them to behave when they are online, and/or using school networks, connections, internet connectivity and devices, cloud platforms and social media (both when on school site and outside of school).
